description: Builds a four note chord from one pitch, with root, third, fifth and seventh on their own outputs and four voices arranged by an inversion and a voicing control

params.text: Transposes the whole chord in semitones, six down at the far left and six up at the far right
Steps the four voices through four inversions, changing which note of the chord becomes the lowest voice
Steps through five voicings, each dropping or raising the second and fourth voice by an octave
Attenuates the offset CV, from nothing to its whole range
Attenuates the inversion CV, from nothing to its whole range
Attenuates the voicing CV, from nothing to its whole range
Lowers the third to three semitones above the root
Lowers the fifth to six semitones above the root
Lowers the seventh to ten semitones above the root
Replaces the root voice with the note two semitones above the root
Raises the third to five semitones above the root
Raises the fifth to nine semitones above the root
Raises the seventh to the octave above the root
Replaces the root voice with the note one semitone above the root
Replaces the root voice with the note three semitones above the root
Lowers the seventh to nine semitones above the root
Raises the fifth to eight semitones above the root

inputs.text: The pitch the chord is built from; the octave is discarded and only the note within it is used
Transposes the whole chord in semitones, scaled by the offset attenuator, 1.5V to a semitone at full
Steps through the inversions, scaled by the inversion attenuator, 3V to a step at full
Steps through the voicings, scaled by the voicing attenuator, 3V to a step at full
A rising edge lowers the third to three semitones above the root
A rising edge lowers the fifth to six semitones above the root
A rising edge lowers the seventh to ten semitones above the root
A rising edge replaces the root voice with the note two semitones above the root
A rising edge raises the third to five semitones above the root
A rising edge raises the fifth to nine semitones above the root
A rising edge raises the seventh to the octave above the root
A rising edge replaces the root voice with the note one semitone above the root
A rising edge replaces the root voice with the note three semitones above the root
A rising edge lowers the seventh to nine semitones above the root
A rising edge raises the fifth to eight semitones above the root

outputs.text: The first voice of the chord, as the inversion and voicing arrange it
The second voice of the chord, as the inversion and voicing arrange it
The third voice of the chord, as the inversion and voicing arrange it
The fourth voice of the chord, as the inversion and voicing arrange it
The root of the chord, within one octave of 0V
The third of the chord, four semitones above the root until an alteration moves it
The fifth of the chord, seven semitones above the root until an alteration moves it
The seventh of the chord, eleven semitones above the root until an alteration moves it

notes: in this build an alteration holds for only the instant its button is pressed or its jack is triggered; the lamp stays lit but the notes go back to the plain chord

inputs.0: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
